annotations.derivable_answer: The three main contributions of SketchSense are: (1) A synchronous RGB–structure framework coupling two branches via Bidirectional Attention Fusion and phrase-level semantic consistency to restore RGB and refined structure; (2) Intrinsic Sketch-Aware Spatial Regulation to adapt sketch attention and fusion across locations and transformer blocks; and (3) Explicit Signed Sketch-Use Modeling using an optional signed spatial prior to express local preservation-or-correction intent when geometry is ambiguous.

supporting_quotations.quote:
In summary, our contributions are threefold:
• We propose a synchronous RGB–structure framework
for interpreting imperfect sketch guidance. Bidirectional
Attention Fusion and phrase-level semantic consistency
couple the two branches, which produce restored RGB
and an observable refined structure. • We introduce Intrinsic Sketch-Aware Spatial Regulation,
which learns to adapt sketch attention and the fusion process across locations and transformer blocks. • We introduce Explicit Signed Sketch-Use Modeling to
express local preservation-or-correction intent when geometry alone is ambiguous, using an optional prior to regulate sketch representation and use.

annotations.rationale: Passage 1 explicitly details the three contributions of SketchSense under an enumerated list.

annotations.derivable_answer: When on-policy distillation is applied to TI2V models, a severe condition-state mismatch arises because the TI2V teacher rigidly requires a clean first frame, but querying it on a student's intermediate T2V rollout forces a clean image condition to coexist with partially denoised frames depicting different content; this unaligned mixture creates temporal discontinuity and causes the teacher to output corrupted velocity fields with contradictory signals that mislead the student toward the image condition rather than refining its own content.

supporting_quotations.quote:
Conversely, recent on-policy distillation methods (Jiang et al., 2026; Zhou et al., 2026) evaluate at student-visited states to offer localized correction, but suffer from a severe condition-state
mismatch in the TI2V setting, as shown in Fig. 3. Rolling out in the T2V mode, the student generates
an internally coherent latent sequence x Stu,(1:F)
t . However, since the TI2V teacher rigidly requires
a clean first frame, querying it on a student’s intermediate state creates a conflicted mixed input:
ˆxMismatch
t = [c img, xStu,(2:F)
t ].(5)
Here, the clean condition c img is forced to coexist with the student’s partially denoised frames, which
depict a completely different, free-running T2V content, causing a severe temporal discontinuity. Essentially, this unaligned mixture constitutes an invalid input state for the model. The teacher
thus outputs a corrupted velocity field, generating contradictory signals that mislead the student’s
denoising process toward c img, rather than refining the student’s own content.

annotations.rationale: Passage 4 provides a comprehensive explanation of the condition-state mismatch failure mode caused by first-frame conditioning in TI2V on-policy distillation.
